title: Employee Onboarding Hub
description: HR and managers: a new-hire portal with 30-60-90 goals, tool access and 1:1s.

spec.useCase: Dana Whitlock runs people operations at a forty-person supply company and uses this so every new hire sees their goals, tools and contacts in one place.

text.text: Welcome. This page is your map for the first 90 days: what to achieve, which tools to get access to, and who to ask. Start with the checklist and your 30-day objectives.
Meet your manager and read the welcome page
Sign in to email, chat and the ticketing system
Harborline Supply keeps small boatyards and marinas stocked with the parts they need, shipped within two days. We are a team of forty who care about being useful and being easy to reach.
Answer the customer first, then fix the process.
Write things down so the next person does not have to ask.
Say what you do not know.
A good first month is mostly listening.
Read the 30, 60 and 90 day plans with your manager in week one.
Tick tool access off as it arrives; chase what is missing by Friday.
Hold a short check-in every week for the first month.
Write down questions as they come up; nobody remembers them by the next meeting.
Chase missing access on Fridays. Each tool row has an owner who can grant it and a button to mark the grant.
Each tool lists who grants access. Ask that person in chat and tick Access granted when it works.
Never share a password in chat. Ask IT for a reset link instead.
Hi, I am starting on [team] and need access to [tool] to do [task]. My manager is [name]. Could you grant it by [day]? Thanks.

Book a 20 minute chat with each person in the first month. Ask what they do, what they wish people knew, and who else you should meet.
Who to ask, by topic. Everyone here has agreed to be asked.
